replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I've always had a bit of a love-hate relationship with mathematics. Back in my school days, I found it challenging but also fascinating. I never excelled at it, but I appreciated its logical structure. Now, as a retired man, I rarely use advanced math, but I still enjoy simple calculations and puzzles.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Not particularly. I've always been more anxious about things like public speaking or complex social situations. Math, to me, is just a set of rules to follow. If I don't understand something, I might feel frustrated, but not anxious.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: No, I haven't used AI for math learning. I'm more of a traditionalist when it comes to learning. I prefer books and face-to-face interactions. Plus, at my age, I'm not very comfortable with the latest technologies.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: Well, first, you need to write the equation in the standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, you can use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a). You need to identify the coefficients a, b, and c, plug them into the formula, and solve for x. Remember to consider both solutions, as there are usually two.

To find stationary points, you first need to find the derivative of the function f(x), which gives you the slope of the tangent at any point x. Then, you set the derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These solutions are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To find the corresponding y-coordinates, you simply plug the x-values back into the original function f(x).
